body:
mike: Quick idea — run a tiny experiment where the edge shim applies tenant-aware routing and local quota checks before hitting the gateway. Keeps high-priority tenant traffic on fast path.

sara: curious — do you mean we evaluate quota at edge (per-tenant tokens) and only forward if tokens available?

mike: yeah, check local token bucket + recent prefix cache. If pass -> route to low-latency pool; if not -> fallback to best-effort pool or enqueue.

aj: how would this interact with console quotas dashboard and billing? we need a single source of truth for usage.

mike: good point. plan is: edge emits compact usage events (tenant, tokens_consumed, route) to a sampling stream. authoritative counters still inside quota service, but edge can short-circuit to reduce load.

lana: worried about consistency — short-circuit could let a tenant exceed committed reserved capacity if clocks drift or events are lost.

mike: mitigation: conservative local tokens (small burst), periodic reconciliation with quota service, and immediate throttles if reconciliation shows overspend. also fallbacks to the dedicated capacity with SLA.

product-ops: from UX side we'd want dashboard flags showing when edge short-circuiting is active per-tenant. otherwise customers will see weird latency/cost changes.

aj: telemetry-wise we should tag traces with route_decision={fastpath,backfill,enqueue}. dashboards can aggregate error-rate and cost delta.

mike: exactly. sample: route_decision + edge_quota_remaining + gateway_latency_ms. that should help signal regressions.

lana: protocol question: do we depend on protobufs at the edge, or keep HTTP+JSON for easier TTL-friendly rewrites?

aj: my vote: keep internal proto on the fastpath for perf, but accept JSON at ingress and transcode at the shim. means shim gets heavier but keeps external ergonomics.

mike: that matches our earlier convo. concern is shim complexity and extra CPU for transcode. we can offload to a small sidecar coderunner to avoid blocking the hot path.

lana: also need to think about auth propagation. tenant headers must be signed or validated to prevent tampering of priority.

mike: use internal signed header + signature TTL. shim verifies signature with edge KMS cache. invalid -> drop or route to verification queue.

product-ops: can we show a canary toggle in console to flip edge short-circuit per-tenant? would help with rollouts.

aj: yes — add a rollout flag on tenant config with percentage rollout and time windows. edge evaluates the flag locally.

mike: we should run a 1% live experiment on low-risk tenants, measure delta in cost/token and P95 latency. target: >=10% latency improvement without >2% over-commit.

lana: test matrix: clock skew simulation, event loss (kafka jitter), and reconciliation spike. need playbook for automatic fallback to gateway if reconciliation fails.

devops-bot: deploy queued: edge-shim-v0.1 -> staging cluster at 2025-11-18T09:00Z (dry-run). :rocket:

mike: staging results will drive proto vs-json decision and thresholds for local tokens. after staging, plan a phased production rollout with dashboard signals gated.

product-ops: add console widget: per-tenant short-circuit rate + reconciliation lag + route_decision heatmap. keep default off for enterprise tenants until validated.

aj: I'll sketch metrics and dashboard layout. mike, can you add a minimal schema for the sampled event? something like: ```
- tenant_id
- route_decision
- tokens_used
- edge_quota_remaining
- reconciliation_offset_ms
- latency_ms
```

mike: will do. also adding `proto_path` flag to decide fastpath encoding. posting a follow-up PR with configs and canary plan.

lana: thanks. one more ask — include a test that intentionally desyncs quota store to ensure the fallback kicks in.

mike: yup. I'll open a thread in #eng-sre for chaos tests.

sara: love it. keep the proposal minimal for initial run: no billing changes, only telemetry + routing.

mike: agreed. follow-up: I'll drop a short RFC and link the staging job here. thanks all. :+1:
